classifications.label: Calibration drift or thermal/mechanical instability in instruments
My cross-check correlations are artifacts of small sample sizes and multiple comparisons
Instruments are measuring genuinely independent physical quantities, or measurement protocol introduces independence by design
Systematic error in my cross-check methodology (lag searches, binning, or alignment)

Instruments are measuring independent physical quantities despite nominal equivalence, or measurement protocol enforces independence by design (electrical isolation, temporal separation, environmental decoupling).
Weak autocorrelations and cross-correlations are statistical artifacts from multiple comparisons (lag searching, offset trials) inflating false-positive rate; no true signal present.

Each instrument exhibits independent 8–13 day cyclic or quasi-periodic noise (thermal cycling, mechanical relaxation, or environmental drift on that timescale), causing weak negative autocorrelations and decorrelation from past readings.

Systematic error in cross-check methodology: lag-search procedure, alignment, or binning introduces spurious correlations or anticorrelations; the uniform weak negative bias reflects methodological artifact, not physics.

Data fabrication, transcription error, or systematic measurement protocol error affecting all four streams identically (e.g., reading instruments in fixed order with timing-dependent bias, or all readings taken under a single hidden constraint).
Instruments measure independent physical quantities despite nominal equivalence; spatial/environmental/temporal isolation enforces decorrelation.
Weak correlations are statistical artifacts from multiple-comparisons bias; true signal is near-zero, consistent with instrument stability and independence.

Each instrument exhibits independent 8–13 day quasi-periodic noise (thermal cycling, mechanical relaxation, or environmental drift), causing weak negative autocorrelations; but this does NOT explain weak cross-correlations between different instrument types.
Systematic error in cross-check methodology: lag-search procedure, timestamp alignment, or binning introduces spurious weak negative bias across all correlations.

Data contamination or measurement protocol error affecting all four streams identically: readings taken in fixed order with timing-dependent bias, or all readings constrained by a hidden single variable.
Systematic error in cross-check methodology: lag-search, timestamp alignment, or correlation computation introduces consistent weak negative bias

Instruments are electrically/mechanically isolated or read under sufficiently different environmental conditions that they capture independent noise sources, not shared signal; weak correlations reflect genuine independence

Multiple-comparisons bias: I tested ~36 correlation hypotheses (6 pairwise pairs × 6 offsets + 4 autocorrelations × multiple lags). At α~0.05 per test, expect ~1.8 false positives; all observed correlations are weak and most within chance thresholds. True signal is near-zero stable instruments.

Environmental quasi-periodicity (8–13 day thermal/humidity cycle) affects all instruments similarly, but instruments are mechanically decoupled enough that phase-locking is weak; weak negative autocorrelations reflect phase opposition within a single cycle
Data contamination or protocol error: all four streams constrained by a hidden single variable or systematic timing-dependent bias in measurement sequencing or transcription
